title: The truth about organic food - according to science | Tim Spector
summary: Nutrition-science podcast where a genetic epidemiologist says organic food has more polyphenols and less cadmium and pesticide, cites cohort links to lower cancer, but says eating fruit and veg matters more and organic is worth prioritising for staples, pregnancy and children.

assertions.quote: are there more nutrients in organic food yes

verdicts.note: Meta-analyses find higher antioxidants and some fatty acids in organic food but no consistent difference in vitamins or minerals and no shown health effect.

assertions.quote: it had around 30 to 40 percent more polyphenols

verdicts.note: The 2014 Baranski meta-analysis found substantially higher polyphenols in organic crops, though study quality and crop variation are large.

assertions.quote: it had less cadmium which is like a toxic mineral

verdicts.note: The Baranski meta-analysis found lower cadmium in organic crops, plausibly from less phosphate fertiliser; results vary by crop and soil.

assertions.quote: the organic food group were protected by about 25 percent

verdicts.note: The NutriNet-Sante cohort linked high organic intake to lower cancer, but it is observational and the larger Million Women Study found no overall reduction.

assertions.quote: it just means the levels will be very much lower
washing helps but it doesn't um but it doesn't get it down anywhere near to organic levels
I haven't given up eating fruits and vegetables when I can't find organic okay to me the large is far outweigh any risk

verdicts.note: Produce intake has large, consistent health associations, while residue risks at typical levels are small and unproven.

assertions.quote: critical times of pregnancy or feeding young children when you know there's so much happening to the body the brain

verdicts.note: Children's higher intake per body weight and developmental sensitivity are real, but no trial shows a health benefit from organic diets at residue levels.
Mother-child cohorts link organic eating in pregnancy to lower pre-eclampsia (OR 0.76), hypospadias and otitis media, but these are observational with likely residual confounding.

Organic milk's lower iodine (147 vs 248 ug/l) makes deficiency more likely for pregnant and breastfeeding women with low dairy intake, a counterpoint for one nutrient rather than a test of the overall claim.

Foetal life and early childhood are called especially vulnerable to neurotoxicants and endocrine disruptors, and children have higher urinary pesticide levels, but no study shows organic diets improve child outcomes.

Higher preconception intake of high-residue produce was associated with lower clinical pregnancy and live birth in IVF patients, driven by pregnancy loss, hinting at a pregnancy-specific risk; it is a small fertility-clinic cohort and organic status of the produce was not recorded.

assertions.quote: they are sprayed just before they're harvested to dry them out okay and so this gives the masses amounts

verdicts.note: Desiccant use close to harvest is the main reason conventional oats and pulses test higher for glyphosate, usually still within legal limits.

assertions.quote: they also had different changes in their gut microbes so the gut microbes were producing different chemicals in response

verdicts.note: Animal studies and one small observational twin study suggest effects, but there is no causal human evidence.

assertions.quote: seems to absorb the herbicides and insecticides on the skin so you don't eat the skin

verdicts.note: Peeled produce such as avocados, onions and bananas shows low residues in the edible part even when grown conventionally.
